name: Norway
summary: Use and possession of narcotics are crimes; small amounts are usually fined. Since 2022, dependent users with small amounts are generally not prosecuted. A June 2025 reform law is not yet in force (Oct 2026).
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Health staff have a duty of confidentiality. Dependent users found with small amounts are generally not prosecuted (2022 guidance).
drugChecking: Free, anonymous drug analysis in Oslo by Foreningen Tryggere Ruspolitikk since 2022 (not state-run). Overdose alerts: overdosefare.no.

lsd.note: Narcotic. Use and possession are crimes; small amounts are usually fined.

mushrooms.note: Psilocybe mushrooms, including spores and dried or prepared mushrooms, are explicitly on the narcotics list.

dmt.note: Narcotic; preparing DMT-containing plants (ayahuasca) is illegal.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is a narcotic; mescaline extracted or prepared from cacti counts as a narcotic.

dox.note: DOB, DOM and related amphetamines are on the narcotics list (individually or via group definitions).

nbomes.note: 25I-, 25B-, 25C-NBOMe and others are on the narcotics list.

2c-x.note: 2C-B and other 2C-x are on the narcotics list.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T-x are covered by the narcotics list (individual entries and phenethylamine group).

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO-DMT, 5-MeO-MiPT and other 5-MeO tryptamines are on the narcotics list.

cannabis.note: Narcotic; small amounts are usually fined, and dependent users generally aren't prosecuted. Medical cannabis only on prescription.

ketamine.note: On the narcotics list: possession or use without a prescription is a crime.

mxe.note: Methoxetamine is on the narcotics list.

dxm.note: Not on Norway's narcotics list (2026). It's a medicine, so sale is pharmacy-regulated and importing it without a prescription is restricted.

nitrous.note: Not a narcotic. Since 1 July 2026, selling it for intoxication or to under-18s is banned, max 17 g per customer per day; consumer imports banned.

amphetamines.note: Narcotics. Dependent users with up to 5 g are generally not prosecuted (2022). ADHD medicines legal with a prescription.

mdma.note: Narcotic; use and possession are crimes, usually fined for small amounts.

cocaine.note: Narcotic. Dependent users with up to 5 g are generally not prosecuted since the 2022 Supreme Court rulings; others are usually fined.

caffeine.note: Legal. Selling energy drinks to under-16s has been banned since 1 January 2026.

alcohol.note: From 18 for drinks under 22% ABV, 20 for stronger. Drinks over 4.7% are sold only at Vinmonopolet.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB, GBL and 1,4-butanediol are all on the narcotics list (industrial use needs a permit).

opioids.note: Heroin and opioid medicines are narcotics; dependent users with up to 5 g heroin are generally not prosecuted. Legal only with a prescription.

tramadol.note: On the narcotics list: possession without a prescription is a crime.

benzodiazepines.note: On the narcotics list: unprescribed possession or use is a crime.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only; harmala/Syrian rue are not on the narcotics list. Ayahuasca is illegal (DMT).

ssris.note: Prescription-only, not narcotics: possession isn't a crime, but unauthorised sale is.
